actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 402 - 16 (Roll no. 55). (text: CR H933-934)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 402 - 16 (Roll no. 55). (text: CR H933-934)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H938-939)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 758.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H933-935)
Mr. Comer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts Postal Service employees and contractors who transport mail, as well as the public accessing safety reports.
dimensions.evidence: Any employee of the Postal Service engaged in the transportation of mail shall report... any contractor... of the Postal Service

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory three-day reporting timelines, standard forms, internal database tracking, potential contractor penalties, and public transparency reports.
dimensions.evidence: subject to appropriate penalties as determined appropriate by the Postal Service, including fines, suspension of contracts, or termination of contracts

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative costs for creating databases and forms, but does not specify explicit appropriation or spending levels.
Requires new USPS regulations, standard reporting forms, a continuous internal digital database, and annual public reporting mechanisms.
dimensions.evidence: issue regulations to require the collection, tracking, and public reporting of information related to deaths and injuries

dimensions.assessment: Permanent ongoing reporting and database maintenance requirements for the Postal Service.

missing_information: Exact figures on the administrative cost to set up and maintain the database and reporting forms.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the U.S. Postal Service to mandate reporting of traffic crashes involving mail transport vehicles that result in injury or death, maintain a digital database, and publish annual public reports.
